APPROVAL OF MINUTES
  EL MONTE CITY COUNCIL REGULAR MEETING
  OF JANUARY 19, 2021

MEETING JOINTLY AND REGULARLY WITH THE EL MONTE HOUSING AUTHORITY; EL
MONTE PUBLIC FINANCING AUTHORITY; EL MONTE WATER AUTHORITY; EL MONTE
PARKING AUTHORITY; SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE FORMER EL MONTE COMMUNITY
REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY; HOUSING SUCCESSOR AGENCY; AND, FROM TIME TO
TIME, SUCH OTHER BODIES OF THE CITY WHOSE MEMBERSHIP IS COMPOSED
EXCLUSIVELY OF THE MEMBERSHIP OF THE CITY COUNCIL

1.  CALL TO ORDER: 6:01 p.m.

2.  ROLL CALL FOR CITY COUNCIL AND AUTHORITY BODIES:

  Jessica Ancona, Mayor/Chair – present
  Maria Morales, Mayor Pro Tem/Authority Member – present
  Victoria Martinez Muela, Councilmember/Authority Member – present
  Alma D. Puente, Councilmember/Authority Member – present

3.  APPROVAL OF AGENDA:

  WITH THE FOLLOWING EDITS/CHANGES TO THE AGENDA:

  Item 14.7 has been pulled.

  m) Mayor Ancona
  s) Mayor Pro Tem Morales  4-0

4.  CLOSED SESSION:

  The City Council and the various Authority Bodies whose membership is composed
  exclusively of the membership of the City Council (collectively, the “Council”) will attempt
  to address and complete all Closed Session business between 6:00 p.m. and 7:00 p.m.
  If the Council completes all Closed Session business prior to 7:00 p.m., the Council will
  take a short recess and commence all Open Session proceedings promptly at 7:00 p.m.
  In the event the City Council is unable to address or complete all agendized Closed
  Session items by 7:00 p.m., the Council will hear all such remaining items toward the
  end of the meeting, immediately following Council Communications. Should any member
  of the public wish to address the Council on any agendized Closed Session matter, the
  Council shall allow such person to address the Council on such matter prior to going into
  Closed Session, provided that all persons wishing to address the Council on an
  agendized Closed Session matter shall fill out a speaker card and be subject to a
  speaker’s time limit of 3 minutes per speaker and further provided that the Council shall
  be under no obligation to respond to or deliberate upon any specific questions or
  comments posed by a speaker or take action on any issue raised by a speaker beyond

such action as the City Council may be lawfully authorized to take on an agendized

8.  PUBLIC COMMENT REGARDING NON-AGENDIZED MATTERS:

  This time has been set aside for persons in the audience to make comments or inquiries
  on matters within the general subject matter jurisdiction of the City Council, the Housing
  Authority, the Financing Authority and/or the Water Authority (collectively, the “Council”)
  that are not listed on this agenda. Although no person is required to provide their
  name and address as a condition to attending a Council meeting, persons who wish to
  address the Council are asked to state their name and address. Each speaker will be
  limited to three (3) continuous minutes. Speakers may not lend any portion of their
  speaking time to other persons or borrow additional time from other persons.

  Except as otherwise provided under the Brown Act (Gov. Code Section 54950 et seq.),
  the Council may not deliberate or take action upon any matter not listed on this posted
  agenda but may order that any such matter be placed on the agenda for a subsequent
  meeting. The Council may also direct staff to investigate certain matters for
  consideration at a future meeting.

  All comments or queries presented by a speaker shall be addressed to the Council as a
  body and not to any specific member thereof. No questions shall be posed to any
  member of the Council except through the presiding official of the meeting, the Mayor
  and/or Chair. Members of the Council are under no obligation to respond to questions
  posed by speakers but may provide brief clarifying responses to any comment made or
  questions posed. The Council may not engage in any sort of prolonged discussion or
  deliberation with any speaker or group of speakers on matters that are not listed on this
  agenda.

  Enforcement of Decorum: The Chief of Police, or such member, or members of the
  Police Department as the Chief of Police may designate, shall serve as the Sergeant-at-
  Arms of any Council meeting. The Sergeant-at-Arms shall carry out all orders and
  instructions given by the presiding official for the purpose of maintaining order and
  decorum at the meeting. While members of the public are free to level criticism of City
  policies and the action(s) or proposed action(s) of the Council or its members, members
  of the public may not engage in behavior that is disruptive to the orderly conduct of the
  proceedings, including, but not limited to, conduct that prevents other members of the
  public from being heard when it is their opportunity to speak or which prevents members
  of the audience from hearing or seeing the proceedings. Members of the public may not
  threaten any person with physical harm or act in a manner that may reasonably be
  interpreted as an imminent threat of physical harm. All persons attending the meeting
  must adhere to the City’s policy barring harassment based upon a person’s race,
  religious creed, color, national origin, ancestry, physical handicap, medical condition,
  marital status, gender, sexual orientation or age.

  Edward Duongo – Good day friends of #CleanAir! The Clean Mobility Team at
  ActiveSGV is pleased to announce the launch of our latest effort to support cleaner,
  greener, and healthier transportation in the San Gabriel Valley! Over the next several
  months we’ll be taking a deep dive in the cities of El Monte and South El Monte to better
  understand the mobility needs of local residents. Cars and trucks are the main source of
  air pollution and greenhouse gas emissions in our region, which remains one of the most
  polluted in the United States. The outcomes of our poor air quality are devastating. High
  rates of asthma and other respiratory illnesses, as well as cognitive impairments, some
  cancers, and even obesity have all been linked to exposure to high levels of air pollution.
  FORTUNATELY, there are more ways than ever to get around without polluting our air.

  4
   City Council Meeting Minutes of January 19, 2021

However as decision-makers consider how and where to invest in transportation
improvements, it’s really important these decisions are informed by the community. In
short, we’re asking you to tell us all about your needs for getting to the places you need
to go! How can you get involved today! Take Our Survey @
www.activesgv.org/mobility4emsem - the first 150 El Monte and South El Monte
residents to take the survey will receive $5 to Cyber Yogurt! Survey available in 4
different languages Clean Transportation Survey (English) (Spanish) (Chinese)
(Vietnamese) Sign-up for a Presentation - If you would like to hear more about this
program and how it can benefit you, your group or community, feel free to contact me at
Ed@activeSGV.org or at 626-539-9146 to schedule a group presentation with Q & A at
the end. For more information about the Clean Mobility project, visit our webpage
http://www.activesgv.org/mobility4emsem. ActiveSGV’s Clean Mobility project is
made possible by funding from the California Air Resources Board (CARB). Thanks
again!

Anonymous – Good evening Mayor and City Council Members. I am a long time resident
of the city of El Monte. My concern is this. A couple of weeks ago I read on Facebook
that the newly elected Mayor of El Monte had been hospitalized for COVID. Which I am
glad she has recovered. But as we all know, many people who contract this virus are not
so lucky. Many of us have lost loved ones due to this highly contagious and deadly virus.
And yet people still continued not take it seriously. So you can only imagine my
frustration and just plain disgust when, a friend of mine that works at Xecora Restaurant,
in The city of El Monte on Peck Rd. and Lower Azusa, mentioned that our newly elected
Mayor Ancona and her guests, patronized the restaurant a week or so before she was
hospitalized for COVID. This friend stated that they heard her personally demand to
have her partying dine inside the establishment. She was told that they could not
accommodate dining inside due to state, county and city restrictions. She arrogantly told
them that nothing would happen to them. She was allowed to dine inside that evening.
This person continued to share that Mayor Ancona and council woman Victoria Martinez
are regulars and like to go dine and drink there. It was not mentioned if Councilwomen
Martínez was also there that night. The party dined and drank till closing. This is
disgusting and clearly already abuse of power. What a reckless disregard for not only
the establishment which was forced to violate the state, county and city ordinances to
appease the newly elected Mayor, but a blatant disregard of what could be hundreds of
lives on the line. Do the rules not apply to her? Clearly morals and ethics are not one of
her big concerns to her as a person or when she’s not the spot light. If our city Mayor
can’t take the lead in setting a good example and showing restraint, will power and
responsibility, then maybe she should step down. Her actions should be address and
reprimanded. This leads me to wonder in what other areas is she abusing her authority?
El Monte residents deserve better. Please take your position as Mayor with the utmost
respect and your authority with the interest of the people you serve and not to serve
yourself. Thank you for your time.

Joe Moreno – We, the undersigned, are retired former school board members to the
Mountain View School District and former union leaders of the California School
Employees Association, Chapter #430. We are out of politics and hope the council
selects a faithful public servant to serve during these challenging times. However, we
have been compelled to speak out about Irma Zamorano’s failed leadership as a board
member and to express that we have NO CONFIDENCE in her being appointed to the
City Council. Zamorano was one of the most unprepared, unethical, incompetent,
employee harassing, and self-serving board members in Mountain View School District's
history. We have no confidence in her holding public office. Zamorano was a one-term
  5
   City Council Meeting Minutes of January 19, 2021

board member in a school district with board members unchallenged because the
community was satisfied with how the board managed the district. Over the last 20
years, she has lost multiple elections for the board and the city except for the one she
narrowly won after a colleague decided not to campaign. She campaigned on the
promise of “change,” like she is doing now, only to vote 100% with the other board
members. Zamorano missed more meetings than all the other four members in her four
years. She rarely attended meetings intended to improve board members’ knowledge of
governance. She talks about being qualified and prepared, but she missed the most
important meeting for a board member, selecting the new Superintendent. Whenever
state officials interviewed our board about our programs, she could not answer and
deferred to the rest of the board. She talks about ethics, but this woman spread
campaign lies about board members accusing people of wrongdoing without evidence.
She is willing to ruin reputations based on false accusations but has never been held
accountable for her lies. She proudly calls herself a diva, as she proved when she
continuously asked for special treatment such as VIP parking at school events and free
food and drinks from our parents fundraising for our students. When the recession was
approaching, the board recognized that cost-saving measures were needed. We agreed
to reduce our individual travel to board conferences, non-essential functions, and
expenses. She insisted on traveling to the eastern United States to attend the National
School Board Conference at taxpayers’ expense. In Zamorano’s four years on the
board, she outspent ALL four other board members on travel. If this wasn’t enough to
disqualify her from public office, she abused her power by following staff members with
her camera, as we hear she does now, bullying, harassing, and intimidating our
employees. It is uncommon in our district for our unions to complain about a board
member's personal actions towards school employees, but this was a common
complaint against her. The council and the community need to know that this woman
should never be allowed back into public office where she will abuse her power and only
serve herself. Zamorano was voted out of office after one term as parents, teachers,
staff, and the community learned that she was not doing her job.

Luis Garcia Bautista – Honorable City Council, Mayor Pro-Tern, City Manager, and

for the hard work you have done to provide resources for the El Monte Community.
During a time of uncertainty, you all have worked hard to ensure that El Monte
residents stay at safely at home and receive basic food assistance. Thank you all
very much! I am writing to you today as a concerned citizen. Over the past few
weeks, we have seen that the First Works Baptist Cult (FWBC) members have
preached hate. From calling LGBTQ+ citizens sodomites to women weak and
submissive, this cult, masquerading as a place of worship, has vilified our

we expected push back from FWBC, what we saw was far worse. Jacob Henry
Lanz, an active member of FWBC physically assaulted one of the protestors on city

without adhering to public safety guidelines. Although the Keep EI Monte Friendly

insurrectionists were fueled by division, weak leadership, and hate speech.
Consequently, they caused the preventable deaths of 5 Americans. Mayor Ancona
released a statement- which she later removed- telling residents that there was

Amanda Mansoorbakht – My name is Amanda Mansoorbakht and I am the journalist
who exposed First Works presence to the greater community. I am also an organizer
with Keep El Monte Friendly. On Sunday, January 17th, El Monte residents came
together to fight bigotry and misinformation with love and unity. Hundreds of people
united in a caravan effort to speak out against the lies, hatred, and violence perpetrated
by First Works Baptist. Weeks of meetings, researching, connecting, and sharing with
fellow community members made this possible. However, Mayor Ancona, your
statement addressing First Works' speech as protected has deeply disturbed many El
Monte residents. Keeping neutral footing regarding this major concern for El Monte
residents, particularly the LGBT community, women, and people of color has major
implications for the physical safety, public health and emotional wellbeing of our
community for generations to come. "There is nothing we can do," is just not good
enough. Mayor Ancona, I am writing this email to demonstrate how First Works
members have not only participated in extremist hate speech but have continuously
been physically violent towards our city. As you already know, First Works members
have continuously threatened the safety of El Mone's LGBT community by encouraging
suicides ("go hang yourself faggot") and the government execution of our community
("we should kills homo like in the middle east") The LGBT is already a high risk
community with the highest numbers for hate crimes, homicides, and suicide. At our
Keep El Monte Friendly protest, First Works member and Mejia henchman, Jacob
Henry, physically assaulted a woman, a peaceful protestor, and her perpetrator was met
with no police enforcement. This was extremely disappointing knowing that Sgt. Luna
discussed with me on three separate occasions that EMPD would remain neutral until
someone's safety was at risk. Sgt. Luna made it clear that our caravan was not to break
any traffic laws yet three different cars were splattered with eggs by First Works
members and received no enforcement. This type of violent behavior is more than
speech. Aside from their violence at the protest, members have repeatedly stalked my
family home and tampered with my mailbox. Yet, the only assurance I received was Sgt.
Luna saying he'll "talk to Bruce about it", as if this is a mere quarrel between Bruce and I.
To a lot of residents this is a fight between safety and peace against violence and
COVID-19 killing more SGV residents. Mayor Ancona and LAPD have not yet addressed
First Works lack of checking temperatures, wearing masks and socially distancing.
Neither have addressed allowing First Works to gather with food or First Works going
door to door, mask less, in low income neighborhoods to "save" the vulnerable
community. Latinos are dying of COVID-19 left and right, why should El Monte let people
who aren't even from El Monte infect our already high risk population? That is imperialist,
gentrification in its most deadly form. The community appreciates the efforts of the city's
distribution of PPE and masks, however these efforts are half baked and appear
disingenuous if the city also allows super spreader indoor gatherings to be protected.
First Works engages in book burning, promotes corporal punishment by stating that
"each child should have a deep fear of their parents", does same day baptisms,
denounces interracial marriages, doesn't allow women to speak, wear pants or makeup,

discourages member's voting and involvement with politics. How many words must I
utter until you hear "this is a violent cult"? Please don't ignore your community's cries for
help. Complacency will be disastrous. Neutrality will be deadly for all of those who get
infected, traumatized, and abused because of First Works. This fight is unprecedented in
El Monte's history and will be recorded for many years to come. I hope the city
government won't be on the wrong side of history.

Mary Ann Powers – At the last council meeting, one of the council members stated that
she could see NO reason to change a decision made by the previous council. I think
there are thousands of reasons to change the decision. 65% of the El Monte voters in
the last election voted for a change. We were tired of the 3 to 2 votes. We didn’t like the
way the 3 council members were voting. We voted for a change. We voted for a council
that could come together. You have an important decision to make by the end of this
month. You have applications to review and interviews to conduct. Make a decision. The
taxpayers of this city cannot afford to pay for a special election. This is an opportunity to
have a councilmember who cares about our community, rather than the concerns of the
developers and cannabis peddlers, who they depend on to provide funds for their next
campaign. The very idea that we would continue with these 2-2 votes for another 10
months only to elect a person who would be in place for 1 year is ridicules. In my
opinion, to keep this seat open in the hopes that a cohort would run for it would a
disgusting abuse of the oath you took.

Kristen Martinez – To the county clerk and council members: This is Kristen Martinez
a doctoral student at UCLA, an employee and resident of El Monte. This church--
First Works Baptist Church on Tyler Ave. needs to get out of the city of El Monte.
The elected officials and law enforcement have been too lukewarm with their
response to the church and have been leaning more toward protecting them. If you
look on social media, the church members mostly males are attacking people and
making fun of gender, sexual orientation, race etc. Many have peacefully protested
while this church has members bullying, mocking and attacking the LGBTQ
community, women, used Anti-Semitism and has been making a mockery of the city.
The Pastor Bruce Mejia is a bully and teaching hateful rhetoric while the whole
congregation is not follow covid 19 protocols and making house visits and large
gatherings. You all need to do something, to put a stop to this and stop sitting on
this. El Monte has a history of the KKK having a post there, do not make another
mistake of a hate group unwanted in this beautiful city. Protect the youth, protect
women and protect families. These members are outsiders coming from different
cities like Long Beach and Montebello, hiding in the "ghetto" as Pastor Mejia has so
eloquently put it. They also physically pushed a female protestor. They call women in
the workforce "whores." Is this what you want people to see of El Monte, or young
children? Act now. Thank you for your time.

Rosanne Bowdry – El Monte is a special city. Sitting on city council you have the honor
of witnessing the American dream unfold before your eyes. El Monte is Home to
generation zero for many families. It’s a city of immigrants and perseverance. It will
always be my home and I take great pride in being from El Monte. But El Monte is not
without its flaws. Broken homes, homelessness and constant reminder that you’re not
good enough. If you can see the smart beautiful people in this city as a treasure we must
protect, you’ll see that Preacher Mejia’s rhetoric is wrong for El Monte. Our city has all
odds stacked against it. Our youth have so many obstacles to “make it out” of El Monte.
So many of my childhood friends have questioned their sexuality and hear constant
homophobic remarks from their families, they’re never allowed to be themselves. Some

  8
   City Council Meeting Minutes of January 19, 2021

even contemplate suicide. It’s our duty to protect El Monte youth. Preacher Mejia has
every right as an American to practice his religion and practice freedom of speech. But
as Council members and guardians of El Monte you need to ask yourself if Preacher
Mejia is good for our city. I personally think he’s a bully and his rhetoric scares me. I fear
for our youth. I fear for the wife that’s beaten every night whose husband is empowered
by words of hate. I fear that words of Preacher Mejia will spark hate in someone’s heart I
fear the next mass shooter whose actions are in their eyes “justified” by Preacher Mejia.
I pray for that soul in First Works Baptist Church that questions their sexuality and would
rather take their life because of his words of hate. Please Declare first Works Baptist
church a hate group and get them out of El Monte Thank you for your time.

Emma Mejia – You should what’s going on with our city, in regards first works Baptist
church. Please take a notice of what the community has done to get him out of our city.
We have a petition with almost 15,000 signatures. That’s accomplishment! Our mayor in
El Monte posted something on her Instagram stating that she can’t do anything because
of his first amendment “freedom of speech.” But she deleted it. As a first time voter for
my city I didn’t expect her to assemble this concern and brush it off. We voted for a new
mayor who can bring change into our lives and city. For Ancona not to even
acknowledge it really is a disappointment. We wanted more from you Ancona. We
wanted your concern, empathy, and take it to the next level as leader. We have proof of
what “the pastor” has done and said to LGBTQ community. Hopefully hearing for the
people have to say. You can have a different perspective! Thank you for your time.

Josh Penney – I will keep this short because I'm sure you have a lot of people writing
and calling in about this. If El Monte doesn't do something about "pastor" Bruce Mejia
and his hatecult at First Works Baptist Church, there is going to be blood on the hands of
the El Monte representatives. The newly elected mayor Jessica Ancona has received a
tidal wave of emails about the goings-on at FWBC and has stated that until a crime is
committed, there's essentially nothing she can do.If there's anything people should have
learned from the political and social unrest that took place in 2020 and the violent
insurrection in D.C. on Jan 6, is that complacency has no place in ethics. To put it
simply, hate speech leads to hate crimes. The longer FWBC is allowed to operate, the
worse it is going to become. By standing idly by you are allowing this hatred to fester
within your community. Stand up for the people who elected you and pay your salary.

Geovani Arrevalo – Hi I live near the City of El Monte. I have proof of one of these men
from the First World Baptist Church saying that he wants to hang everyone on Sunday. I
will attach the screenshots of the messages from Instagram. My overall concern that I
want the city council to hear is that I worry that this type of hateful rhetoric will eventually
lead to a hate crime or murder in our city. Bruce Mejia does not work alone and has
many men behind him. Many people who attend his sermons believe that it would be
okay to execute anybody who is LGBTQIA+. We cannot let this happen. These people
are being brainwashed by a man who is twisting the bible. This is not a regular church
that preaches love and tolerance. This is a church that discriminates and denigrates
LGBTQIA+ individuals by calling us "dirty faggots, pedophiles, and disgusting
sodomites" that are not worthy of basic human dignity or respect. We don't want to
change their beliefs. We just want them to stop preaching hate in front of children,
posting it on Youtube for other people to see, and harassing us online and wishing us
death. How can we go about removing their institution from our community? How do we
keep El Monte safe? Do we have to wait until one gets killed or attacked when the police
are not there to protect?

Jasmine N. – I wanted to bring to your attention, if not brought to it already, a so called
"church" in El Monte that goes by First Works Baptist Church. The pastor and his
followers are promoting hate against the LGBTQ community and against women. He
uses homophobic, transphobic, misogynistic slurs in every sermon. Referring to the
LGBTQ community as freaks, faggots and sodomites and also refers to women as weak
an inferior to men. He has even gone as far as to refer to Disney characters or
princesses to be whores. I truly believe with this church in the community, it is an unsafe
environment for our LGBTQ community, and also women in the community. His
following is cult like and has no regard for anyone who is not like them. Please feel free
to contact me with any questions, below is my contact information.

Cosmic J. Menes – I write to you today as a long-time resident of the City of El
Monte. I have lived in our fair city for 69 years, and in that time, I have seen good
times and I have seen bad times. During the good times the common thread was a
council that truly had the residents' interests of our city in mind. During the bad times
the common thread was a council that had their own interests in mind. Currently I
feel that half of our council-Mayor Ancona and Councilwoman Martinez- Muela do
not have our best interest at heart. I have seen Councilwoman Martinez-Muela bully
former councilwoman Macias on and off the dais, besmirch the good name of former
councilwoman Wallach, and hypocritically offer her thoughts and prayers when Mrs.
Wallach passed. Joined on the dais by her good friend Mayor Ancona, the
beginnings of a fiefdom are coming into focus. Ancona isn't much of a leader, having
